asr_text: What would the world be like if the landmasses were instantly rotated by 90 degrees? It would profoundly alter our world in general and the weirdly Minnesota-heavy world of 1990s

cinema in particular. We're assuming that all the material is magically shifted around, so there are no massive tsunamis or earthquakes. Even so, it would definitely still be a catastrophe. The ice caps would melt long before new ones could
and if Michael Bay were telling the story, then, as the waters of the Gulf of Mexico began to cool, and the Mississippi slowed and became an estuary, the region's wildlife would spread inland.
And one morning, all those Minnesotans we know from 90s cinema would wake up to the site of
floating rafts of fire ants, followed by 5 million lost hungry alligators, who would wallow in the
mighty docks now melted skating rink. Add yet more for the characters and grumpy old men to complain about and lead to a similarly gruesome, if more reptilian, ending to the movie Fargo.
